IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NOS. 13388-13389 OF 2026
(@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CIVIL) NOS.21392-21393 OF 2026)
VIJAY GANAPATI APPELLANT(S)
 VERSUS
CHITRA GANAPATI RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
Heard the petitioner in-person.
2. From the records it transpires that the sole
respondent had refused to accept the notice sent by this
Court and thus, notice on her stood deemed to have been
served.
3. Leave granted.
4. The appellant is aggrieved by the order impugned dated
23.01.2026 passed in Civil Revision No.691/2026 by which
permission to amend his pleadings with regard to bringing
on record the details of the immovable property held by
his late father and for incorporation of a relief based on
the judgment in the probate case dated 24.02.2021, has
been partly allowed, inasmuch as, the amendment has been
allowed only with regard to his pleadings relating to
immovable property, but not for incorporation of the
1

probate judgment. Review application filed against the
said order was also dismissed vide order dated 19.03.2026
in Review Application No. RA-CR-15/2026, which is also
impugned herein.
5. It was submitted that the parties are the adopted
children of Late Shri. R. Ganpati and upon his death, the
appellant had filed a Suit for injunction and declaration
against the respondent with regard to a property, which
according to him, was required to be divided equally among
both the parties. In the said Civil Suit the respondent
had filed a Will dated 20.12.2000 bequeathing the
appellant's share in the suit property in favour of the
respondent. This prompted the appellant to seek amendment
in his plaint disputing the Will which was allowed.
However, in the meantime, the respondent-defendant sought
probate of the Will which was executed according to her by
her late father on 20.12.2000. The same upon trial was
dismissed by judgment dated 24.02.2021 and according to
the appellant, the same had attained finality. The
appellant then moved the Trial Court under Order VI Rule
17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 seeking amendment
of the plaint by seeking to incorporate a relief based on
the judgment dated 24.02.2021 passed in the probate
proceedings.
6. The Trial Court dismissed the said application and the
High Court in CR No. 1335/2025 directed the Trial Court to
2

pass fresh order after considering all the pleas raised by
the appellant.
7. The Trial Court by order dated 01.10.2025 partly
allowed the prayer of the appellant to amend his pleadings
with regard to the movable properties and the share
claimed therein but disallowed the amendment sought
pertaining to incorporation of the probate judgment. The
review petition filed by the appellant was also dismissed
on 18.10.2025.
8. Thereafter, the appellant moved before the High Court
by filing Civil Revision No.691/2026 in which the impugned
order has been passed.
9. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that once
the probate sought by the respondent had been dismissed,
such fact is a necessary issue for consideration in the
Suit filed by the appellant and not allowing incorporation
of such plea in the plaint, will cause damage to the
appellant's case, that too, when clearly the law is in his
favour.
10. We have considered the matter and gone through the
material on record. In view of the dismissal of the Suit
seeking probate of the Will in favour of the respondent
having attained finality, and also in the written
statement in the suit filed by the appellant, the
respondent has placed reliance on the said Will, we find
that the judgment of the Court dated 24.02.2021 dismissing
3

the Suit for probate of the Will was required to be
brought on record and rightly by way of an amendment as
sought by the appellant.
11. For the reasons aforesaid, the appeals are allowed.
The amendment as sought by the appellant stands allowed.
Consequences to follow.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.
.....................J.
(AHSANUDDIN AMANULLAH)
....................J.
(MANMOHAN)
NEW DELHI
OCTOBER 05, 2026
